Tests for {@link BritishCutoverChronology} and {@link BritishCutoverDate}.

Britain switched from the Julian calendar to the Gregorian calendar in September 1752. Wednesday 2nd September 1752 (Julian) was immediately followed by Thursday 14th September 1752 (Gregorian), skipping 11 days. The dates 3rd through 13th September 1752 never existed in British history.

Key rules verified by these tests:

  • Before the cutover (up to 2 Sep 1752): Julian calendar — leap year every 4 years with no century-year exception, meaning 1700 is a leap year in this calendar.
  • From the cutover (14 Sep 1752 onwards): Gregorian calendar — century years not divisible by 400 are not leap years (e.g. 1800, 1900 are not leap years).
  • The cutover gap (3–13 Sep 1752): Dates in this range are treated leniently as Julian dates and shifted forward by 11 days to produce a valid Gregorian date.
  • Year 1752: Has only 355 days because 11 days were removed in September.
The ISO (Gregorian) LocalDate corresponding to the first day after the British cutover gap. In British calendar terms this is also 14 September 1752.
No CLDR calendar type is defined for this calendar system

Addition test cases: start date, amount, unit, and expected result.

Column layout: [year, month, dom, amount, unit, expectedYear, expectedMonth, expectedDom, bidi]

The {@code bidi} (bidirectional) flag indicates whether the same data row can also verify subtraction: when {@code true}, subtracting {@code amount} from the expected date should yield the original date (used by {@link #test_minus_TemporalUnit}). Rows with {@code bidi=false} represent cases where adding lands in the cutover gap, so the result is shifted — and subtracting from that shifted result would not reverse to the exact original date.
Adding DAYS around the cutover gap (Sep 2 → Sep 14 is one calendar day)
-1 day crosses back over the gap
Adding WEEKS (7 days × n, crossing or straddling the cutover gap)
+7 days from Sep 2 = Sep 20 (gap consumes 11 days)
Adding MONTHS (calendar months; landing in the gap shifts result forward)
Aug 12 +1 month = Sep 12 → gap → Sep 23 (not reversible)
Oct 12 -1 month = Sep 12 → gap → Sep 23 (not reversible)
Larger time units (years, decades, centuries, millennia, eras)
switching from AD to BC era

Verifies subtraction by reusing the {@code data_plus} data set in reverse.

The parameter order from {@code data_plus} is reinterpreted here: the "expected" position (first three columns) becomes the subtraction start, and the "input" position (columns 6–8) becomes the expected result. The {@code bidi} flag guards rows where the addition was non-reversible (e.g. because the result was shifted out of the cutover gap).
